pr_title: Add special handling for use of 'to_json' in templates
pr_body:
<!--

-->
## Breaking change
This could prevent us from converting a template to a native type where we would expect to if the logic isn't well scoped


## Proposed change
It looks like the move to support native types in templates broke the `to_json` filter. An object gets serialized to JSON during rendering using `to_json` but then we parse the result using `literal_eval` which converts it back to an object. Through some testing, I found that `to_json` uses `"` in the rendered string whereas native jinja rendering uses `'`. I've added some guard logic that returns the originally rendered result (e.g. not passed through `literal_eval`) when a certain set of conditions are met. I am open to suggestions on how this logic should be implemented as the current implementation seems fragile.

issue_context.title: When using `to_json` filter in a template, sometimes voluptuous validation fails "template value should be a string for dictionary value @ data['message']"
issue_context.body:

  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
I am trying to pass the data from an event into a `persistent_notification` by passing "{{ trigger.event.data|to_json}}" to the message parameter of the `persistent_notification.create` service. For some payloads, this works as intended, but for others, the schema validation fails: "template value should be a string for dictionary value @ data['message']"

This event data gets converted properly:
```json
 "data": {
        "lockname": "front_door_lock_manager",
        "state": "unlocked",
        "action_code": 4,
        "action_text": "RF Unlock",
        "usercode": 0,
        "usercode_name": null
    }
```

This event data results in the error:
```json
"data": {
        "lockname": "front_door_lock_manager",
        "state": "unlocked",
        "action_code": 5,
        "action_text": "Keypad Lock",
        "usercode": 1,
        "usercode_name": "R and S"
    }
```

I am not clear why the behavior is different in each case.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2020.12.1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): N/A
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): OS
- Integration causing this issue: `persistent_notification` integration or `template` helper
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/persistent_notification/

## Relevant automation logic:
```yaml
 id: '1609129371655'
  alias: Test
  description: ''
  trigger:
  - platform: event
    event_type: keymaster_lock_state_changed
  condition: []
  action:
  - service: persistent_notification.create
    data:
      title: test
      message: '{{ trigger.event.data|to_json }}'
  mode: parallel
  max: 10
```
